title: Mashrabiya Lattice Joinery
summary: Mashrabiya is the carved and turned wooden lattice of Arab windows and balconies, built from small spindles, beads and star-shaped pieces slotted together without nails so that light and breeze pass through a geometric web.
howToPlay: Choose a wood or glass colour and a piece from the strip under the frame.
Touch a square to fit that piece: it is repeated in all matching places of the frame, because a lattice repeats around its centre.
Copy the small screen shown above the frame, then press Check.
rules: The frame is symmetric left to right, top to bottom and along both diagonals, so every piece you fit is copied to its seven partners.
A square counts only when both the piece and the wood or glass colour match the screen.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Wooden lattice screens have shaded windows and balconies in Cairo, Damascus and many other towns of the Arab world for centuries; joiners still turn and fit the pieces by hand in workshops.
credits: Pattern design: World Heritage Games (original lattices after traditional turned-spindle screens)
